facts.claim: In a four-party card scheme, a card payment moves from the payer’s account to the payee’s through the scheme, an issuer on the payer’s side and an acquirer on the payee’s side (EU Regulation 2015/751, Article 2).
Under EU Regulation 2015/751 (Article 3), the interchange fee on a consumer debit card payment may be at most 0.2% of its value.
Under EU Regulation 2015/751 (Article 4), the interchange fee on a consumer credit card payment may be at most 0.3% of its value.
The EU’s interchange fee rules call interchange fees a main part of the fees acquirers charge merchants (Regulation 2015/751, recital 10).
For each card payment the issuer, for the cardholder, pays the acquirer, for the merchant; the interchange fee flows the other way, from acquirer to issuer (ECB Occasional Paper 131, 2011).
Visa’s guide for US merchants says each approved authorisation reduces the cardholder’s available funds, a hold, and that authorisations a merchant won’t complete must be reversed.
An IETF Internet-Draft (draft-ietf-httpapi-idempotency-key-header, not yet an RFC) has the client send a unique Idempotency-Key so the server can recognise a retry and not repeat the operation.
EU Directive 2015/2366 (PSD2, Article 97) requires strong customer authentication when a payer starts an electronic payment.
Strong customer authentication uses two or more independent elements: something only the user knows, something only they have, and something they are (PSD2, Article 4(30)).
Under Delegated Regulation 2018/389 (Article 16), a remote payment of at most €30 may skip strong authentication, while payments since the last one total at most €100 or number at most five.
Under the same regulation (Article 18), a payment rated low-risk in real-time analysis may skip strong authentication, up to €500 if the provider’s card fraud rate is at most 0.01%.

EMV 3-D Secure shares payment and device data between merchant and issuer so the issuer can authenticate the shopper: many just click Buy, higher-risk ones face a challenge such as a one-time passcode.
Visa’s dispute guide for merchants (October 2026) says a fully authenticated 3-D Secure payment is protected from fraud disputes; a payment without 3-D Secure is not.
Visa groups dispute reasons into four categories: Fraud, Authorization, Processing Errors and Consumer Disputes.
Under the PCI card security standard (requirement 3.4.1), screens and reports show at most the first digits and last four of a card number, unless a documented business need justifies more.
